title: "Access Data"
date: today

## Overview

Approved files are available from the `FDP` server on **datalibweb**, in two collections:

| Collection | Content |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `FDPRAW` | Raw survey microdata, questionnaires and documentation |
| `FDP` | Harmonized microdata (50by35 schema) and harmonization programs |

The harmonized welfare module in the `FDP` collection is called **`WELF`**.

## Steps at a glance

Data users can choose R or Stata. The steps are the same.

1.  **Request access.** Register on datalibweb and subscribe to the required surveys ([Step 1](#sec-access-permission)).
2.  **Save the token.** Install the client and save the datalibweb token ([Step 2](#sec-access-token)).
3.  **Find the survey.** Check what is available for the country of interest ([Step 3](#sec-access-find)).
4.  **Load the data.** Download the harmonized file into R or Stata ([Step 4](#sec-access-load)).
5.  **Calculate the self-reliance rate** (optional) ([Step 5](#sec-access-sr)).

## Step by step

### Step 1. Get access {#sec-access-permission}

Register on datalibweb and request access to the `FDPRAW` and `FDP` collections. Access is private by default: each user subscribes to the datasets they need and is approved by an admin. An admin can also make a collection public, so that all (internal) datalibweb users can use it without subscribing.

Both clients need the World Bank intranet or VPN.

### Step 2. Save the token once {#sec-access-token}

Two clients are available: the [`datalibweb` Stata package](https://github.com/worldbank/datalibweb) and the [`dlw` R package](https://github.com/worldbank/dlw). Install the one in use, then save the datalibweb token. It is the same token PRIMUS uses. It is valid for 30 days and renewed on the [datalibweb website](https://datalibweb2.worldbank.org). Do not commit tokens or put them in scripts.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

``` r
dlw_set_token("<datalibweb token>")   # one-time setup; stored in the system keychain
```

R reuses the saved token. Run `dlw_set_token()` again only after renewal.

## Stata

``` stata
datalibweb, token(<datalibweb token>) version(2)
* one-time setup; do not hard-code it in a do-file.
```
:::

### Step 3. Find the survey {#sec-access-find}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

``` r
library(dlw)

# all collections (servers) the user can access
dlw_server_catalog()

# what is in a collection; in R the FDP server holds both the harmonized
# files and the raw files they were built from
dlw_server_catalog("FDP")

# everything available for one country, across collections
dlw_country_catalog("TCD")

# files for one country within a collection
dlw_server_inventory("TCD", server = "FDP")
```

## Stata

``` stata
* interactive browser: click through region -> country -> collection
datalibweb
```
:::

### Step 4. Load the data {#sec-access-load}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

``` r
library(dlw)

# harmonized 50by35 welfare module (WELF) from the FDP collection
welf <- dlw_get_data(
  country_code = "TCD",
  filename     = "TCD_2022_EHCVM_V01_M_V01_A_FDP_WELF.dta",
  server       = "FDP",
  year         = 2022
)

# a raw file from the FDPRAW collection; year and survey (acronym) disambiguate
# the specific survey vintage, the R equivalent of Stata's surveyid()
raw <- dlw_get_data(
  country_code = "TCD",
  year         = 2022,
  survey       = "EHCVM",
  filename     = "individual_TCD_2022.dta",
  server       = "FDP"
)
```

## Stata

``` stata
* harmonized 50by35 welfare module (WELF) from the FDP collection;
* the latest master and harmonization versions are loaded by default
datalibweb, country(TCD) years(2022) type(FDP) mod(WELF) clear

* pin specific vintages for replicability
dlw, country(TCD) years(2022) type(FDP) mod(WELF) verm(01) vera(01) survey(EHCVM) clear

* a raw file from the FDPRAW collection
datalibweb, country(TCD) years(2022) type(FDPRAW) ///
    surveyid(TCD_2022_EHCVM_V01_M) filename(individual_TCD_2022.dta) clear
```
:::

Versions are **never replaced**: a new release gets a new version number and earlier vintages stay available. The full survey ID used in an analysis should be recorded with it (see [File naming conventions](#sec-access-naming)).

### Step 5. Calculate the self-reliance rate {#sec-access-sr}

The self-reliance rate is the weighted share of people whose `welfare_self` reaches the poverty line. When the file has a national poverty line (`natpovline`) and no currency conversion is needed.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

``` r
# weighted share with welfare_self at or above the national line
if ("natpovline" %in% names(welf)) {
  weighted.mean(welf$welfare_self >= welf$natpovline, welf$weight)
}
```

## Stata

``` stata
* weighted share with welfare_self at or above the national line
capture confirm variable natpovline
if !_rc {
    gen byte _sr = welfare_self >= natpovline
    sum _sr [aw=weight]
}
```
:::

`natpovline` is optional and some files do not have it (nothing is calculated then). For the \$3.00/day international line, the poverty rate, and the camp / non-camp results, see [Full indicator calculation](#sec-access-full).

### If something goes wrong

| Symptom | Meaning | Action |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Access denied, or the collection is not listed | The user is not subscribed to the collection | Request access in Step 1 |
| Token or login error | The datalibweb token has expired | Get a new token and repeat Step 2 |
| Cannot connect | The computer is off the World Bank network | Connect to the intranet or VPN |
| No survey found | The survey is not approved yet, or the country or year is wrong | Check [Step 3](#sec-access-find), and ask the uploader whether it is approved |
| `natpovline` not found | The survey has no national poverty line | Use the international line instead (see below) |

## Reference

### File naming conventions {#sec-access-naming}

datalibweb survey identifiers guarantee replicability: versions are **never replaced** — new releases get a new version number, and previous vintages remain available. Always record the full survey ID used in an analysis.

**Raw (master) data** in `FDPRAW`:

```         
CCC_YYYY_SSSS_V##_M
```

- `CCC` — 3-letter ISO/WDI country code (e.g. `COL`)
- `YYYY` — year data collection started
- `SSSS` — survey acronym (e.g. `GEIH`, `EHCVM`, `RHS`)
- `V##_M` — version of the **master** (original) data; first release is `V01`

**Harmonized data** in `FDP`:

```         
CCC_YYYY_SSSS_V##_M_V##_A_FDP
```

- `V##_A` — version of the harmonization (**adaptation**), independent of the master version
- `FDP` — the collection of harmonized surveys

**Module files** append the module name to the survey ID. The 50by35 harmonized welfare file (V01) for Chad is:

```         
TCD_2022_EHCVM_V01_M_V01_A_FDP_WELF.dta
```

### Full indicator calculation {#sec-access-full}

This example loads a harmonized file and calculates the self-reliance rate and poverty rate, in percent, on the national line (primary, if `natpovline` is in the file) and the \$3.00/day 2021 PPP line, for the whole sample and by camp status. Each estimate comes with a **standard error and 95% confidence interval**. It uses the same CPI and PPP helpers, and therefore the same values, as the [indicator XML](03-harmonized-upload.qmd#sec-cpi-ppp) in the harmonized upload. Unlike the steps above, it needs a copy of this repository: it loads `R/utils.R` (R) or `Stata/utils.do` (Stata) by relative path, so run it from the repository's main folder, or copy that one file next to the script and edit the path.

The standard errors account for the survey design:

- **Clusters** are the primary sampling units (`psu`) when the file has them, with no missing values. Otherwise they are households (`hhid`), because members of a household share one `welfare` value and cannot be treated as independent observations. Ignoring this makes the standard errors far too small.
- **Strata** (`strata`) are used when the file has them, with no missing values.
- **Subgroups** such as camp are estimated as subpopulations of the full design, never by dropping the other rows first, which would give wrong standard errors.
- **Confidence intervals** use a t distribution with the design's degrees of freedom (number of clusters minus number of strata).
- A subgroup whose rows fall in a single cluster has no estimable standard error. R reports `NA`; Stata reports a standard error of about zero, which should be ignored.

The R example needs the [`survey`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=survey) package; the Stata example uses the built-in `svy` commands.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

``` r
library(dlw)
library(survey)
source("R/utils.R")   # dlw_support_tables(), dlw_cpi_ppp(); run from the repository root

# harmonized 50by35 welfare module (WELF) from the FDP collection
welf <- as.data.frame(dlw_get_data(
  country_code = "TCD",
  filename     = "TCD_2022_EHCVM_V01_M_V01_A_FDP_WELF.dta",
  server       = "FDP",
  year         = 2022
))

ccode <- welf$code[1]
yr    <- welf$year[1]

# CPI and PPP from the latest datalibweb Support files (2021 framework):
# CPI is the survey-year CPI relative to 2021 (1 in 2021); PPP is the ICP 2021
# conversion factor (LCU per international $).
fx <- dlw_cpi_ppp(dlw_support_tables(), ccode, yr)

# poverty line in $/day 2021 PPP (placeholder — pending confirmation)
zline <- 3.00

# ---- indicators: 0/100 variables, so that their mean is a percentage -------
# self-reliance uses welfare_self; poverty uses welfare
welf$sr_intl <- 100 * (welf$welfare_self / 365 / fx$cpi / fx$ppp >= zline)
welf$hc_intl <- 100 * (welf$welfare      / 365 / fx$cpi / fx$ppp <  zline)

# primary indicator: national poverty line, if natpovline is in the file.
# natpovline shares welfare's annual per capita LCU basis, so no CPI/PPP.
if ("natpovline" %in% names(welf)) {
  welf$sr_nat <- 100 * (welf$welfare_self >= welf$natpovline)
  welf$hc_nat <- 100 * (welf$welfare      <  welf$natpovline)
}
inds <- intersect(c("sr_nat", "hc_nat", "sr_intl", "hc_intl"), names(welf))

# ---- survey design ----------------------------------------------------------
# clusters: psu if available and complete, otherwise households; strata if
# available and complete
has <- function(v) v %in% names(welf) && !anyNA(welf[[v]])
options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")   # strata with a single psu
design <- svydesign(
  ids     = if (has("psu")) ~psu else ~hhid,
  strata  = if (has("strata")) ~strata else NULL,
  weights = ~weight, nest = TRUE, data = welf
)
cl <- if (has("psu")) welf$psu else welf$hhid

# ---- estimates with standard errors and 95% CIs ----------------------------
est <- function(d, label, rows) {
  m  <- svymean(reformulate(inds), d)
  ci <- confint(m, df = degf(design))
  out <- data.frame(group = label, indicator = inds, estimate = coef(m),
                    se = SE(m), ci_low = ci[, 1], ci_high = ci[, 2], row.names = NULL)
  # a standard error needs at least two clusters in the group
  if (length(unique(cl[rows])) < 2) out[c("se", "ci_low", "ci_high")] <- NA
  out
}
res <- est(design, "All", rep(TRUE, nrow(welf)))

# by camp status, as subpopulations of the design
# (camp may be missing for every row in some surveys, e.g. COL)
camp <- as.integer(welf$camp)
for (l in sort(unique(camp[!is.na(camp)]))) {
  res <- rbind(res, est(subset(design, camp %in% l),
                        c("Non-camp", "Camp")[l + 1], camp %in% l))
}
print(res, digits = 4)
```

## Stata

``` stata
* harmonized 50by35 welfare module (WELF) from the FDP collection;
* the latest master and harmonization versions are loaded by default
datalibweb, country(TCD) years(2022) type(FDP) mod(WELF) clear

* calculate SR indicator
local ccode = code[1]
local year  = year[1]

* CPI and PPP from the latest datalibweb Support files (2021 framework):
* CPI is the survey-year CPI relative to 2021 (1 in 2021); PPP is the ICP 2021
* conversion factor (LCU per international $). Needs the datalibweb token set
* in Stata; run from the repository root.
do "Stata/utils.do"
dlw_cpi_ppp, country(`ccode') year(`year')
local cpival = r(cpi)
local pppval = r(ppp)

* poverty line in $/day 2021 PPP (placeholder — pending confirmation)
local zline 3.00

* ---- indicators: 0/100 variables, so that their mean is a percentage -------
* self-reliance (_sr_*) uses welfare_self; poverty (_hc_*) uses welfare
gen double _sr_intl = 100*((welfare_self/365/`cpival'/`pppval') >= `zline')
gen double _hc_intl = 100*((welfare/365/`cpival'/`pppval') < `zline')
local inds _sr_intl _hc_intl

* primary indicator: national poverty line, if natpovline is in the file.
* natpovline shares welfare's annual per capita LCU basis, so no CPI/PPP.
capture confirm variable natpovline
if !_rc {
    gen double _sr_nat = 100*(welfare_self >= natpovline)
    gen double _hc_nat = 100*(welfare < natpovline)
    local inds _sr_nat _hc_nat `inds'
}

* ---- survey design -------------------------------------------------------------
* clusters: psu if available and complete, otherwise households; strata if
* available and complete
local clustervar hhid
capture confirm variable psu
if !_rc {
    quietly count if missing(psu)
    if r(N) == 0 local clustervar psu
}
local stratavar
capture confirm variable strata
if !_rc {
    quietly count if missing(strata)
    if r(N) == 0 local stratavar strata
}
if "`stratavar'" != "" {
    svyset `clustervar' [pw=weight], strata(`stratavar') singleunit(centered)
}
else {
    svyset `clustervar' [pw=weight], singleunit(centered)
}

* ---- estimates with standard errors and 95% CIs --------------------------------
svy: mean `inds'

* by camp status, as subpopulations of the design
* (camp may be missing for every row in some surveys, e.g. COL)
quietly levelsof camp, local(camplevels)
foreach l of local camplevels {
    di as result "camp==`l'"
    svy, subpop(if camp==`l'): mean `inds'
}
```
:::
